questions.statement: The text says families began storing rainwater 'before anyone suggested it'. What can be inferred?
questions.context: A text reports that families built water tanks on their roofs years before the official programme was announced.

options.text: The need was obvious to the residents before the official programme existed.
options.feedback: Correct! The timing of the tanks shows the residents recognised the problem on their own.

options.text: The residents had been told what to do by the committee.
options.feedback: The phrase says the opposite: nobody had suggested it at the time.

options.text: The programme failed because nobody used the tanks.
options.feedback: The text says the practice spread, which contradicts a failure.

options.text: The committee was created after the tanks were bought.
options.feedback: The tanks predate the committee, which the wording makes explicit.

questions.explanation:
An inference combines what the text states with a reasonable conclusion. The timing shows the problem was perceived before any official action.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The writer calls the old wells 'the bones of the valley'. This phrase suggests that the wells are:
questions.context: A text describes ancient wells as 'the bones of the valley' in a passage about the region's water history.

options.text: dangerous and should be closed immediately.
options.feedback: The image does not convey danger; the wells are described as essential.

options.text: old and fundamental to the life of the place.
options.feedback: Correct! The image of bones conveys age and a supporting role, which is exactly the suggestion.

options.text: recently built by the committee.
options.feedback: The wells are ancient, so the image contradicts the idea that they are recent.

options.text: the only source of income in the valley.
options.feedback: The image suggests importance for survival, not for income.

questions.explanation:
A metaphor expresses an idea rather than a fact. This image compares something hidden and essential to the structure that supports a body.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text says the water committee 'wrote down the figures before deciding anything'. What does this show about the group?
questions.context: A text describes how a local water committee reached its decisions during the dry months.

options.text: It ignored the opinions of the residents.
options.feedback: The text describes the opposite, since the rules were agreed with the residents.

options.text: It changed the figures whenever it was convenient.
options.feedback: Nothing in the text suggests that any figure was altered.

options.text: It based its decisions on evidence.
options.feedback: Correct! Recording the figures first shows that the decisions rested on evidence rather than on preference.

options.text: It preferred intuition to measurement.
options.feedback: The practice described is measurement, not intuition.

questions.explanation:
Recording the figures before deciding shows a deliberate method. The order of the two actions is what carries the meaning, and that is what the reader has to infer.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The author writes that the youngest families 'kept the buckets under the beds'. What is the likely reason?
questions.context: A text describes poor families in a water-short town hiding their water containers inside the house.

options.text: To decorate the room for visitors.
options.feedback: The text describes a problem of supply, not decoration.

options.text: To keep the buckets out of reach of children at play.
options.feedback: Keeping buckets out of reach would be about safety, and the text stresses the shortage.

options.text: To store the buckets during a flood in the street.
options.feedback: No flood is mentioned anywhere in the account.

options.text: To protect a small supply from evaporation or theft.
options.feedback: Correct! In a shortage, hiding the stored water protects it, which is the most likely reason.

questions.explanation:
Purpose has to be inferred from context. A text that presents a shortage makes the reason for hiding water understandable to the reader.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which inference is NOT supported by the text about the committee?
questions.context: A text describes a local committee of residents that meets regularly to review water agreements.

options.text: It was created by the national government.
options.feedback: Correct! The text presents the committee as a local body and never attributes its creation to the national government.

options.text: It meets on a fixed schedule.
options.feedback: The fixed schedule is stated in the text.

options.text: It reviews the agreements with the community.
options.feedback: The reviews of agreements are exactly what the meetings are for.

options.text: It is made up of residents of the town.
options.feedback: Membership by residents is described when the committee is introduced.

questions.explanation:
An unsupported inference is one the text never licenses. Local origin, a fixed schedule and community membership are all stated, while national creation is not.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text says the programme 'failed in the villages without tanks'. What can be inferred?
questions.context: A text compares villages that installed storage tanks with villages that did not, and reports different results.

options.text: The residents of those villages did not want to save water.
options.feedback: The text does not blame the residents; it names the absence of tanks as the difference.

options.text: The infrastructure, not the people, was the decisive factor.
options.feedback: Correct! The contrast shows that the physical installations, not the attitudes of the people, decided the outcome.

options.text: Those villages had more water than the others.
options.feedback: The text implies those villages suffered more, so they did not have more water.

options.text: The committee refused to help the villages without tanks.
options.feedback: The text describes a technical limitation, not a refusal to help.

questions.explanation:
The contrast between the two groups isolates the variable. When only the infrastructure differs, the conclusion points to the infrastructure.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The writer mentions 'the sound of the pump at dawn'. Why include this detail?
questions.context: A text uses a sensory image of the pump at dawn in a passage about daily life in a dry region.

options.text: To prove that the pump was broken that morning.
options.feedback: A sound at dawn shows activity, not a breakdown.

options.text: To show that the villagers worked in a factory.
options.feedback: A village pump is part of daily life and has nothing to do with a factory.

options.text: To make the routine and the value of the water vivid.
options.feedback: Correct! The image gives the reader a concrete sense of the routine and of what the water means to the people.

options.text: To indicate that the village had too much water.
options.feedback: The whole text is about scarcity, so the detail cannot signal abundance.

questions.explanation:
Sensory details make a routine concrete for the reader. The detail is chosen because it carries the meaning of the passage.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text states that prices of bottled water rose sharply. What can be inferred?
questions.context: A text describes an economic consequence of a water shortage affecting ordinary households.

options.text: The government stopped the sale of bottled water.
options.feedback: The text says nothing about a prohibition on bottled water.

options.text: Everyone in the region bought a pump.
options.feedback: Buying a pump is mentioned as an option, not as something everyone did.

options.text: The wells recovered during that year.
options.feedback: The wells yielded less water during that period, so they did not recover.

options.text: Households felt the shortage in their budgets as well.
options.feedback: Correct! The price rise shows that the shortage also reached the economy of the households.

questions.explanation:
A rise in prices is presented as a consequence of the shortage, and it affects the households the text is describing.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The author says the rules were 'simple enough to be remembered and strict enough to be respected'. This shows that the rules were:
questions.context: A text evaluates a set of community agreements and explains why they were designed in that particular way.

options.text: Well designed for the community that has to follow them.
options.feedback: Correct! The two qualities described, easy to remember and strict enough to be obeyed, show careful design.

options.text: Too complicated for the people who wrote them.
options.feedback: The text says the rules were simple, not complicated.

options.text: Ignored by everyone after the first month.
options.feedback: The text says they were respected, which is the opposite of being ignored.

options.text: Imposed without the agreement of the residents.
options.feedback: The rules were agreed in a public meeting, so they were not imposed without consent.

questions.explanation:
A writer's own comment about a solution is the strongest evidence of how effective it considered that solution to be.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which inference can be drawn about the people who left the region?
questions.context: A text notes that several families of a dry village left the area during the worst years of the shortage.

options.text: They moved away to find better schools.
options.feedback: The text says nothing about schools as a motive.

options.text: The lack of water was one of the reasons they moved away.
options.feedback: Correct! The departures coincide with the worst years of the shortage, so the water is a reasonable cause.

options.text: They were forced to leave by the national government.
options.feedback: No government action is mentioned, and the text presents the shortage as the cause.

options.text: They left because the wells produced too much water.
options.feedback: The wells produced less water, not more.

questions.explanation:
The timing of the migration coincides with the shortage, so the shortage is a reasonable explanation the text licenses.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text says a technician 'spent a whole day on the pump'. What does this suggest?
questions.context: A text reports the time a technician needed to restore a water pump in a village.

options.text: The technician was careless with his time.
options.feedback: The text reports a fact about the job, not an attitude of the technician.

options.text: The pump was working perfectly well.
options.feedback: A working pump would not need a day of attention.

options.text: The repair was slow and the water system fragile.
options.feedback: Correct! A whole day on one repair suggests a fragile system and a slow recovery.

options.text: The village had more than one pump.
options.feedback: The text mentions a single pump, so there is no evidence of others.

questions.explanation:
A long task signals difficulty. The reader is expected to connect the hours spent with a system that is old and easily breaks down.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which inference about rainfall is best supported by the text?
questions.context: A text compares rainfall records across several decades in a dry region.

options.text: It increased steadily during the period described.
options.feedback: A decline, not an increase, is what the records show.

options.text: It never changed at all in the region.
options.feedback: The text is concerned precisely with a change over the years.

options.text: It is measured only in the capital city.
options.feedback: The measurements concern the region, not one city.

options.text: It became less reliable over the recorded years.
options.feedback: Correct! The comparison across decades shows that rainfall became less dependable.

questions.explanation:
A pattern reported over many years is the evidence from which a trend can be inferred. The text points to a decline in reliability.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The writer says the tank 'looks like a small house on the roof'. This comparison is meant to:
questions.context: A text describes a water tank installed on a roof in a village.

options.text: Help the reader picture a structure much bigger than expected.
options.feedback: Correct! The comparison with a building gives a sense of size, which a measurement would not convey as quickly.

options.text: Show that tanks are made of wood.
options.feedback: The material of the tank is not what the comparison conveys.

options.text: Warn that roofs are dangerous to build on.
options.feedback: The text warns about the shortage, not about the safety of roofs.

options.text: Compare the tank with a school building.
options.feedback: The comparison is with a house, not with a school.

questions.explanation:
A simile gives the reader a mental image. The comparison with a small house shows the size of the object without giving measurements.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text says a family 'sold a goat to buy a tank'. What can be inferred?
questions.context: A text describes the sacrifices a household made to obtain a water storage tank.

options.text: The family had plenty of money to spare.
options.feedback: The sale of an animal is the opposite of having money to spare.

options.text: The tank was a serious financial sacrifice for them.
options.feedback: Correct! Selling livestock to buy a tank shows a real sacrifice, not spare money.

options.text: The tank was given away by the committee.
options.feedback: The text says the family bought the tank, not that it was given away.

options.text: The family had no livestock after that year.
options.feedback: The text does not say they lost every animal, only the one they sold.

questions.explanation:
Selling a productive animal is presented as a cost. That detail lets the reader judge how much the solution mattered to the family.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which inference about education is best supported by the text?
questions.context: A text reports that long walks to fetch water reduced the time children could spend in class.

options.text: The schools were better funded than before.
options.feedback: The text says nothing about school funding.

options.text: The region stopped teaching children altogether.
options.feedback: Children kept attending, but less often, so schooling was not stopped.

options.text: The shortage interrupted the schooling of many children.
options.feedback: Correct! Fewer hours at school because of the walk to fetch water is a direct consequence described in the text.

options.text: Attendance improved with the arrival of the tanks.
options.feedback: The text presents the shortage as a barrier to schooling, not as an improvement.

questions.explanation:
A consequence described in the text is an inference the reader can draw without leaving the information given.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The author says the new rules were 'copied from an older village'. This implies:
questions.context: A text reports that a town adopted agreements that another community had already been using.

options.text: The older village had solved the same problem successfully.
options.feedback: Adopting proven rules is a deliberate choice, not an inability to design any.

options.text: The older village had no water at all.
options.feedback: The older village used the rules precisely because it had water to manage.

options.text: The new rules were written by a foreign organisation.
options.feedback: The origin given is another village, not a foreign body.

options.text: The community could not design its own arrangements.
options.feedback: Correct! A set of rules that another village kept successfully was worth copying, which the wording implies.

questions.explanation:
Copying a workable solution is evidence that it worked. The reader is invited to treat the older village as a successful precedent.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can be inferred from the fact that the text lists the names of several committee members?
questions.context: A text about local water management names several of the people who served on the committee.

options.text: The committee was a real group of identifiable residents.
options.feedback: Correct! Naming real residents shows that the committee existed as a group of people.

options.text: The committee met only once in fifty years.
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence suggests that the committee met only once.

options.text: The members were appointed without election.
options.feedback: The text does not say how the members were chosen.

options.text: The text is a fictional story about imaginary people.
options.feedback: The specific names indicate a documented account, not a fictional one.

questions.explanation:
Named individuals in an informational text indicate that the account is documented rather than invented. The detail anchors the story in reality.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The text says the programme cost 'less than one tank in the capital'. This comparison is used to:
questions.context: A text argues in favour of a low-cost local water programme by comparing its price to a single structure elsewhere.

options.text: Show that the capital ignored the problem.
options.feedback: The text is not criticising the capital; the comparison is only about scale.

options.text: Show that the measures were cheap and affordable.
options.feedback: Correct! Comparing the cost to a familiar item shows the programme is cheap enough to be affordable.

options.text: Show that the programme failed for lack of money.
options.feedback: A low cost is presented as an advantage, not as the cause of failure.

options.text: Show that the committee was dishonest.
options.feedback: No dishonesty is suggested anywhere in the text.

questions.explanation:
A comparison with something familiar makes an abstract figure understandable. Here the effect is to show that the programme is affordable.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which inference about the future is best supported by the text?
questions.context: A text describes a water programme that succeeded in a village and states the condition for its continuation.

options.text: The region will never face another shortage.
options.feedback: The text presents a risk, so it cannot promise that no shortage will return.

options.text: The wells will be replaced by new ones next year.
options.feedback: No replacement of the wells is announced in the text.

options.text: The measures can work if the community keeps following them.
options.feedback: Correct! The text ties the success of the measures to the community's continued cooperation.

options.text: The committee will be dissolved once the tanks are full.
options.feedback: The text presents the committee as permanent while the rules are in force.

questions.explanation:
A text that states a condition for success licenses an inference about the future that keeps that condition, and no more.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The writer places the story of the old well at the end of the text. This choice suggests the author wants to:
questions.context: A text about a water programme ends with a brief recollection of a well that has been in use for generations.

options.text: Introduce the topic of the text for the first time.
options.feedback: A closing paragraph cannot introduce a topic for the first time.

options.text: Present evidence that the programme failed.
options.feedback: The closing image is positive, so it does not present failure.

options.text: Add a completely unrelated anecdote.
options.feedback: The well is directly related to the water supply, so the anecdote is not unrelated.

options.text: Close with an image that links the past to the present.
options.feedback: Correct! Ending with an old well links the historical depth of the practice to the present programme.

questions.explanation:
Position is part of the message. A closing image that returns to the past pulls the argument together and gives it a lasting tone.
---
questions.subject: ingles
